phase2a.excluded_scope: Phase 2B hardware claims, Host/JSON-RPC/WebSocket/service/UI, firmware, Vision, ECS, public C ABI, bindings, and packages remain outside this candidate

transitions.cause: not-delivered settlement evidence claims cancel, deadline, or parent close
not-delivered settlement evidence claims cancel, deadline, or parent close

timeouts.wait_timeout: ends only the caller wait and never cancels the operation
timeouts.operation_deadline: records immutable cancellation intent and wakes the settlement owner; only not-delivered evidence claims Cancelled with reason deadline, while already accepted effect evidence may still claim Succeeded
timeouts.protocol_timeout: fails the operation in the controller error domain after a bounded handshake or ACK exchange
timeouts.transport_write_timeout: bounds partial report and command writes independently from protocol replies

operations.terminal_commit: exactly once after a legitimate settlement owner atomically consumes mutually exclusive evidence and claims one winner; immutable result and error are mutually exclusive

terminal_transaction.intent: the first Requested, Deadline, or ParentClose reason is immutable and only signals the owner; intent alone never claims a winner or moves outstanding work onto a path that excludes Succeeded
terminal_transaction.claim: the registered settlement owner consumes EffectAccepted, NotDelivered, or ExecutionFailed evidence and claims the matching winner in one arbiter critical section; only that same owner with identical evidence and candidate may reclaim its abandoned deferred transaction, while other claimers fail closed; claim publishes no event, unlink, or waiter notification
terminal_transaction.child_admission: the parent cancellation node is sealed before owner cleanup; admission linearized after sealing is rejected and previously admitted children are cancelled
order: consume mutually exclusive settlement evidence and claim one winner
close and cancel the admitted cancellation subtree
complete fallible owner cleanup outside operation and arbiter locks
record cleanup settlement outside operation and arbiter locks
commit one immutable terminal state and terminal event

cleanup_projection.success: cleanup Ok preserves Succeeded; cleanup Err or panic becomes Failed with the cleanup error
cleanup_projection.failure: cleanup Err or panic is secondary and the original failure remains primary
cleanup_projection.cancellation: Requested, Deadline, and ParentClose each preserve the immutable first reason while cleanup Err or panic remains secondary

terminal_transaction.handoff: handoff is allowed once only when a transferable owner was pre-held before work, the original owner task is joined, and all cleanup plus settlement evidence is in the shared record
terminal_transaction.ownership_loss: without a joined legitimate owner, pre-held transferable owner, and shared evidence, close reports CloseFailed while preserving the non-terminal operation, registry identity, and waiter state with no terminal event, unlink, or notify
terminal_transaction.failure_isolation: cancellation tree sealing transfers hook and child ownership without invoking hooks or dropping user captures while operation state, cancellation hooks, or children locks are held; hook invocation, discarded capture destruction, child ownership release, and panic payload destruction are isolated per item, so one fault never truncates sibling hooks or child propagation; event, registry, hook, reentrant destruction, or poisoned-lock faults never skip registry unlink or waiter notification

runtime.explicit_close: the only deterministic shutdown path; an external caller owns the Active to Closing transition and every concurrent or later caller receives the same saved Closed or Failed CloseOutcome
runtime.reentrant_close: a resource callback running on the deterministic close owner thread receives CloseOwner before waiting when it synchronously re-enters close on the same Runtime; the outer close continues to the one saved outcome
runtime.final_handle_drop: synchronously rejects admission and requests root cancellation only; it never waits, invokes resource close callbacks, joins tasks, spawns a finalizer thread, closes event production, or promises RuntimeClosed
runtime.supervised_tasks: tasks are created only through Runtime supervised spawn; Runtime registers before body execution, binds owner automatically, shares one consumable completion and JoinHandle ownership with the returned task handle, joins and unregisters, rejects same-Runtime synchronous close from the task before state changes, and lets explicit task join wait for TLS destructors and OS thread exit even after nondeterministic Runtime storage release
runtime.close_failure: resource, task, event, registry, or settlement-ownership failure commits one saved CloseFailed diagnostic after all safe later close phases finish; a legitimate transferable owner with shared evidence still settles before a task-panic report, while ownership loss preserves the non-terminal operation and registry without waking its waiter

generic_deadlines.target: absolute target_ns in the owning Runtime Clock epoch; an already-due target is Fired before registration returns
generic_deadlines.identity: Runtime-local registration IDs increase monotonically and are not reused while observable
generic_deadlines.independence: a registration is not an Operation, resource, or supervised task and allocates no OperationId, emits no operation event, and changes no public registry count
generic_deadlines.system_clock: the shared deadline worker fires without consumer or domain-lane progress, wakes to recompute after earlier registration or disarm, and wakes one registered poll_resolution observer after committing its outcome
generic_deadlines.virtual_clock: only clock advance wakes due entries; equal target_ns entries commit in registration-ID order before any observer notification, and dispatch records follow notification
generic_deadlines.close: close seals admission first, keeps existing registrations serviced through resource cleanup, external owner join, and legal Operation settlement, then commits remaining Armed entries as RuntimeClosed before notifying observers and joining the worker

close_order: enter Closing and seal work plus deadline admission
publish RuntimeClosing and cancel the root tree
close resources in Runtime ID order while the deadline worker remains active
join ordinary supervised and external owner tasks while the deadline worker remains active
settle operations through their joined legitimate owner or one pre-held transferable handoff and preserve ownership loss
resolve remaining deadlines as RuntimeClosed and join the internal deadline worker
verify operation, resource, and active-task registries after internal worker join
save the Closed outcome, enter Closed, and notify close waiters

events.single_reader: each subscription admits one active reader; a concurrent reader fails immediately with ResourceBusy without consuming an event
events.overflow: oldest ordinary events are summarized by EventGap; authoritative state remains queryable
events.close: RuntimeClosed bypasses subscriber severity and log filters and is emitted only after successful cleanup, task join, and registry convergence; CloseFailed uses runtime.close_failed as the final event; either final event leaves subscriptions drainable and rejects later publish attempts; Drop alone emits neither final event

controller.report_interval_scope: every report, including cancellation and close neutralization
controller.direct_success_boundary: the unique backend final-byte completion owner reserves the shared settlement gate before Clock, telemetry, or hook work; that reservation protects the accepted ordinary-direct winner, and later publication claims Succeeded so cancellation or close intent cannot rewrite it

serial.identity: stable device-instance identity is independent from optional labels and COM reassignment
serial.optional_properties: VID, PID, manufacturer, and friendly name are present only when supplied by Windows; COM names never imply device identity
serial.io: open, partial read/write, zero progress, absolute deadline, operation/resource cancellation, busy/access denied, timeout, and disconnect are normalized inside easycon-serial
serial.close: resource-close cancellation wakes pending overlapped I/O; close settles cancellation and releases every event, HANDLE, stream, and owner synchronously; failed serial neutralization invalidates the stream before operation terminal commit
serial.dependency_direction: easycon-serial implements ControllerTransport as a system leaf; controller/runtime/model never depend on a concrete serial backend or Win32

amiibo.retry: header and payload ACK failures use bounded caller-selected reset-and-retry cycles for the same chunk
amiibo.limits: slot count and maximum data length are rejected unless supplied through explicit Hardware Unverified capability limits
amiibo.cleanup: partial failure, cancellation, deadline, disconnect, and resource close preserve one terminal outcome and bounded reset or stream-close cleanup

sequence.origin: monotonic time when the command lane acquires the sequence
sequence.offsets: absolute from origin and monotonically non-decreasing
sequence.same_offset: apply in input order and emit one merged report
sequence.drift: targets never derive from the previous dispatch
sequence.cancel_or_failure: remove pending steps, accept a neutral report when connected, then release lease and commit terminal state
sequence.phase2a_acceptance: VirtualClock executes 10,000 input steps with exact order, same-offset merge, no early report, absolute targets without cumulative drift, one terminal event, and operation/resource/task registry convergence

controller.automation_lease: exclusive Controller-only primitive: asynchronous acquire resolves Granted, Cancelled, Deadline, Closed, or Failure on one record with Cancelled > Deadline > Closed > Failure > Granted priority; each non-zero generation seals action admission before one paced neutral release settles as accepted, stream-settled not-delivered, or explicit cleanup failure; the unique backend final-byte completion reserves that release record before Clock, telemetry, or hook work, so a close after reservation requires one independent final paced neutral; a legitimate Controller lane owner with completion and stream-settlement evidence completes affected action/release waiters exactly once with Err(cleanup_failure), while lane ownership loss with no transferable owner or evidence preserves their nonterminal record and requires Runtime CloseFailed; Controller close takes over an Undispatched or Outstanding release record before the backend gate, while a GateClaimed or retained Committed lane-owned record requires one independent final paced neutral; a release record registered after close admission seal completes only after its closed stream is settled; ECS is outside this milestone

classifications.rule: button, HAT, stick, handshake, and 7-bit report bytes match the audited source
sequence timing uses validated absolute monotonic offsets instead of the source constructor defect
cancellation and failure neutralize before terminal observation and lease release is observable
late ACK generations cannot complete a later request
save uses 20-byte chunks with seven-bit offset/length fields and 0x90; select uses 0x91; both require 0xff ACK
